raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44758. With `--linear-attn-prefill-backend nvidia_kda`, Kimi-K3 prefill returns NaN after about 1,800 tokens. Triton is correct on the same inputs.

The A_kk inverse kernel inverted each 16x16 diagonal block with a power series on bf16 operands. When beta is close to 1 and the keys are similar, the terms of the series get large and bf16 loses the result. The inverse was wrong in every chunk, so the recurrent state grew each chunk until it overflowed. Against an fp64 reference, every stage before the inverse matches.

## Modifications

- Invert the diagonal blocks by forward substitution with fp32 arithmetic. L is still read as bf16, and the off-diagonal blocks still use bf16 MMA. The output layout is unchanged.
- Add `test_nvidia_prefill_correlated_keys`: similar keys, beta near 1, slow decay, a partial last chunk and a nonzero initial state. It fails on main and passes here. The existing test uses random keys, which do not hit this.

## Accuracy Tests

Issue repro (`minimal.pt`, 2,048 tokens):

| | NaN rows | max abs diff vs fp32 reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 256 (from row 1792) | 1.2e37 |
| this PR | 0 | 1.9e-4 |
| Triton | 0 | 1.4e-4 |

The inverse now stays within 7.5e-3 of an fp64 inverse in every chunk. `test_kda_prefill.py` passes on B200 and B300 (the PTX tests skip on B200).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`chunk_kda_fwd`, H=8, median of 3 rounds:

| | B200 32k | B200 8k | B300 32k | B300 8k |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | 1315.9 us | 350.8 us | 1260.0 us | 337.4 us |
| this PR | 1325.5 us (+0.7%) | 357.9 us (+2.0%) | 1266.5 us (+0.5%) | 341.0 us (+1.1%) |

nodes.body:
@samridh10exe thanks a lot for the quick fix and for digging into the A_kk inverse, great find! tested it end to end on HGX B300 with full Kimi-K3 (TP8/EP8, fp8 KV, MegaMoE, sglang v0.5.21 + only your kernel change), batched cold prompts so the nvidia_kda path actually runs:

| prefill batch | main: broken answers | this PR | triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 x 8,192 | 8-10 / 10 | 0 / 10 | 0 / 10 |
| 4 x 4,096 | 17-18 / 20 | 0 / 20 | 0 / 20 |
| 8 x 2,048 | 38-40 / 40 | 0 / 40 | 0 / 40 |

single cold 128K prompt unchanged (4.90 s). one separate thing we noticed: the 8 x 2,048 batch takes ~5.3 s on nvidia_kda with or without this PR vs ~0.7 s on triton.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

-Akk 64×64 Lower Triangular Block Inversion — Full BF16.
+Akk 64×64 Lower Triangular Block Inversion.
 
-BF16 input, BF16 SMEM (packed bf16x2), BF16 MMA m16n8k16 (FP32 accum), BF16 output.
+BF16 input, BF16 SMEM (packed bf16x2), BF16 output. Diagonal blocks are
+inverted with FP32 arithmetic, off-diagonal blocks with BF16 MMA m16n8k16
+(FP32 accum).

-  (I+L)⁻¹ = (I-L)(I+L²)(I+L⁴)(I+L⁸)   [L strictly lower triangular, L¹⁶=0]
+  Diagonal 16×16 blocks: (I+L)⁻¹ by forward substitution in FP32

   - 4 warps (128 threads) per CTA, each CTA processes one 64×64 Akk matrix
   - sAkk [64,36] fp32 — each FP32 slot holds packed bf16x2 (stride 36)

   - cp.async: BF16 global → packed bf16x2 in FP32 SMEM (raw bytes align)

+  - BF16 MMA m16n8k16 with FP32 accumulator for the off-diagonal matmuls

   - C→A chain: cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 to pack FP32 accum → bf16x2 A-operand
